executionStatus: The contract, process and browser cases below are specifications, not executed tests.
boundary: Offline; no real model API, Jira, Bitbucket, deployment, merge or production repository writes.

requirements.name: Intake and accepted requirements
requirements.requirement: Preserve source identity, local refinements and explicitly accepted scope.

requirements.name: Role selection and custom specialists
requirements.requirement: Select specialists by need and preserve reusable definitions in immutable assignments.

requirements.name: Model routing and assignment
requirements.requirement: Route exact configured identities, enforce assignment policy and expose the model actually used.

requirements.name: External messages and observation
requirements.requirement: Use independently observable external delivery between separate agent processes.

requirements.name: Process lifecycle and recovery
requirements.requirement: Run distinct observable processes, stop them accurately and recover boundedly from durable state.

requirements.name: Scheduling and dependencies
requirements.requirement: Respect one coding ticket, three compatible specialists, one writer and verified merge dependencies.

requirements.name: Repository ownership and work products
requirements.requirement: Use isolated owned worktrees, preserve user work and record exact source revisions.

requirements.name: Validation and review gates
requirements.requirement: Readiness requires criteria coverage, real check results and independent review for the exact current revision.

requirements.name: Jira, PR and human handoff
requirements.requirement: Synchronize allowed updates, reconcile uncertain writes and retain the human merge gate.

requirements.name: Supervision and truthful presentation
requirements.requirement: Let one operator supervise through the coordinator while seeing actual specialist activity and durable history.

requirements.name: Offline containment and authority
requirements.requirement: Keep secrets server-side, restrict local mutations and prevent untrusted content from granting authority.

requirements.name: Time, usage and bounded execution
requirements.requirement: Persist execution limits and represent incomplete accounting accurately.

cases.title: Site-aware upsert
cases.action: Import equal issue keys/IDs from two sites, then refresh one.
cases.expected: Two tasks remain distinct; only that site's imported fields change; local notes, criteria and history survive.
cases.evidence: Database snapshots before/after import.

cases.title: Board and queue order
cases.action: Refresh Jira rank while reordering the local queue.
cases.expected: Board follows imported rank; execution order follows local priority.
cases.evidence: Persisted rank/position plus API responses.

cases.title: Optional Explore and Grill
cases.action: Run one accepted ticket directly; Explore and Grill two others.
cases.expected: Direct Run is allowed; Explore/Grill persist notes without launching coding work.
cases.evidence: Run count, notes and launch ledger.

cases.title: Accepted brief versions
cases.action: Edit a brief after queueing and again during execution.
cases.expected: Queued and active snapshots retain their versions; changed scope requires an explicit decision before affected work continues.
cases.evidence: Brief versions, assignment snapshots and decision record.

cases.title: Conflicting Jira refresh
cases.action: Change upstream requirements during work against an accepted brief.
cases.expected: Affected work pauses for a decision; neither side silently overwrites the other.
cases.evidence: Conflict record and dispatch log.

cases.title: Explicit repository scope
cases.action: Use two configured repositories; submit missing and multiple targets.
cases.expected: One target is required per coding ticket; mappings never change silently; no cross-repository dispatch.
cases.evidence: Validation response and worktree registry.

cases.title: Research-only outcome
cases.action: Request an evidence-backed design assessment without code changes.
cases.expected: Produce the requested artifact and limitations; no fabricated commit, coding check or PR is required.
cases.evidence: Artifact manifest and zero repository/provider mutations.

cases.title: No automatic backlog execution
cases.action: Import a backlog and queue one selected item; replay Run twice.
cases.expected: Only the selected item starts; duplicate requests do not create duplicate active runs.
cases.evidence: Queue/run uniqueness and launch count.

cases.title: Minimal versus complex team
cases.action: Provide a small bug brief and a complex UI/security/domain brief with scripted selection proposals.
cases.expected: Small work uses a small team; complex work admits justified specialists within scheduler limits; neither launches the whole catalog.
cases.evidence: Selected roles, reasons and launch history.

cases.title: Custom role lifecycle
cases.action: Create, edit, disable and insert a custom specialist using an isolated configuration path.
cases.expected: Validation is enforced; a valid inserted role gets a real assignment at a safe point; disabled roles cannot receive new work.
cases.evidence: Config revisions and assignment events.

cases.title: Immutable definition snapshot
cases.action: Change a role's model and instructions after assignment.
cases.expected: Existing assignment keeps its definition/model revision; only a new explicit assignment uses the update.
cases.evidence: Stored snapshots before/after edit.

cases.title: Project constraints
cases.action: Assign the same role to two projects with different instructions and allowed tools.
cases.expected: Each assignment includes its own project constraints; reusable defaults remain unchanged.
cases.evidence: Prompt/config snapshots and tool permissions.

cases.title: Reviewer independence
cases.action: Ask the implementer to review its own change, then assign a distinct reviewer using the same model.
cases.expected: Self-review cannot satisfy the gate; a separate non-implementer assignment can, even with the same model.
cases.evidence: Implementation provenance and review author assignment.

cases.title: Reporter versus writer
cases.action: Ask the delivery reporter for a Jira milestone and technical writer for a repository guide.
cases.expected: Reporter uses bounded Jira permissions; writer edits only its authorized repository scope and respects the single-writer lease.
cases.evidence: Tool grants, effect ledger and changed paths.

cases.title: Invalid selection proposal
cases.action: Return unknown/disabled/duplicate roles or an unauthorized infrastructure role from the selector.
cases.expected: Validate the proposal; reject invalid assignments before any process or privileged tool starts.
cases.evidence: Rejected proposal and zero unauthorized launches.

cases.title: Complete catalog binding matrix
cases.action: Bind each catalog role plus coordinator/reporter to every captured selector in a pure assignment test.
cases.expected: All 950 bindings preserve provider, full model ID and role identity; dispatch eligibility is a separate capability/policy decision.
cases.evidence: Parameterized results with fixture and assignment hashes.

cases.title: Heterogeneous and rotated teams
cases.action: Execute baseline, heterogeneous and rotated scripted profiles.
cases.expected: Every launch receives its pinned model; role selection is independent of assignment; no coordinator model leaks into specialists.
cases.evidence: Assignment, launch, runner-reported and stub-request identities.

cases.title: Slash-bearing IDs and API dispatch
cases.action: Use slash-bearing model IDs and aperture-bedrock-compat selectors.
cases.expected: Split at the first slash only; use captured API family rather than guessing from provider name.
cases.evidence: Exact request route and payload assertions.

cases.title: Missing, stale and ambiguous selectors
cases.action: Remove a pinned model, duplicate a selector and request a fuzzy alias in derived fixtures.
cases.expected: Reject ambiguity; preserve the original snapshot; stale/missing catalog evidence is visible; no guessed replacement.
cases.evidence: Validation errors and unchanged assignment.

cases.title: Default model resolution
cases.action: Leave a role's model empty, resolve the run default, then change the external default.
cases.expected: Resolve and persist one explicit selector before launch; restart cannot silently change it.
cases.evidence: Resolution record across restart.

cases.title: Effort validation
cases.action: Try default/low/medium/high and unsupported efforts against declared model metadata.
cases.expected: Resolve default explicitly; reject unsupported medium for low/high-only models; do not send reasoning settings to a no-reasoning model.
cases.evidence: Requested/resolved effort and stub payload.

cases.title: Capabilities and context limits
cases.action: Request images from a text-only model, unknown tool support, and inputs at/over declared limits.
cases.expected: No name-based capability inference; unknown stays unknown; preflight blocks or records an explicit safe adaptation before dispatch.
cases.evidence: Capability provenance, budget calculation and dispatch decision.

cases.title: Runtime identity mismatch
cases.action: Make OMP report or send a different model than the assigned selector.
cases.expected: Mark mismatch and stop affected work before side effects; never report the requested identity as observed.
cases.evidence: Observed state/request versus assignment and pause record.

cases.title: Explicit fallback
cases.action: Inject a retryable provider failure with and without a configured fallback policy.
cases.expected: Only a compatible policy-approved fallback is used; create a new recorded attempt; otherwise escalate; no silent model swap.
cases.evidence: Attempt lineage, fallback reason and effect counts.

cases.title: Advisory router boundaries
cases.action: Return a scripted JEV/System 1-style recommendation that violates budget, capability or review policy.
cases.expected: Treat it as a proposal; hard constraints still hold; advisory failure leaves deterministic configured selection available.
cases.evidence: Proposal, validation and routing decision.

cases.title: Secondary OMP model paths
cases.action: Enable simulated prewalk/planning/summarization defaults that differ from the assignment.
cases.expected: Inventory and pin or disable secondary model calls; no unrecorded hidden model/provider dispatch.
cases.evidence: Complete provider request log, including secondary requests.

cases.title: Provider error taxonomy
cases.action: Inject 401, 403, 429, timeout, disconnect, malformed result, empty final and exhausted auto-retries.
cases.expected: Classify errors, bound retries and backoff, preserve uncertainty; prompt completion alone cannot prove a useful result.
cases.evidence: Raw sanitized events, attempt counters and no false success.

cases.title: Four-hop external round trip
cases.action: Run coordinator → specialist 1 → specialist 2 → specialist 1 → coordinator with three subprocess fixtures.
cases.expected: Four addressed messages and replies originate in the assigned processes; external receipts and recipient events agree.
cases.evidence: Distinct process/session IDs, four envelopes and delivery ledger.

cases.title: Passive observer
cases.action: Observe all events with two readers while recipients receive messages.
cases.expected: Reading never consumes delivery; readers can reconnect and reconstruct history.
cases.evidence: Observer cursors versus recipient acknowledgements.

cases.title: Duplicate delivery
cases.action: Deliver the same message and correlation ID twice before and after recipient restart.
cases.expected: Transport may repeat; domain handling and resulting effects occur once; duplicates remain auditable.
cases.evidence: Inbox dedupe keys and effect counts.

cases.title: Reordering and causality
cases.action: Deliver replies before acknowledgements and replay an old attempt's late result.
cases.expected: Correlate by run/assignment/attempt and message IDs; do not advance an unrelated or replaced assignment.
cases.evidence: Causal event trace and rejected stale message.

cases.title: Lost send acknowledgement
cases.action: Persist a message then drop the send reply before the sender crashes.
cases.expected: Reconcile by stable identity before retry; one logical send survives; unknown delivery stays unknown.
cases.evidence: Outbox, mailbox records and reconcile results.

cases.title: Receive crash windows
cases.action: Crash before inbox persistence, after persistence, after processing, and before transport acknowledgement.
cases.expected: Durable inbox/application records support recovery; no loss or repeated side effect at any window.
cases.evidence: Crash-point trace and durable records after reopening.

cases.title: Mailbox restart and expiration
cases.action: Restart the message service, simulate downtime, then expire an undelivered message.
cases.expected: Reconnect with bounded backoff; retention/idempotency limits are visible; expiry does not mean delivered or task complete.
cases.evidence: Mailbox/outbox history and attention state.

cases.title: Routing and isolation
cases.action: Send to unknown recipients, another run and an obsolete attempt; inject a forged sender.
cases.expected: Reject or quarantine unauthorized routing; never wake the wrong assignment.
cases.evidence: Authorization decisions and recipient launch log.

cases.title: Polling and payload boundaries
cases.action: Exercise idle polling, burst sends, 429s, oversized messages and malformed envelopes.
cases.expected: Respect bounded poll/backoff policy; preserve pending messages; reject invalid payloads; no busy loop.
cases.evidence: Fake-clock request counts, backlog and error events.

cases.title: Process independence
cases.action: Launch coordinator and two specialists; terminate only one specialist process.
cases.expected: Distinct OS processes and sessions remain observable; surviving agents continue or wait according to dependency state.
cases.evidence: Process registry, liveness and independent output streams.

cases.title: Specialist replacement
cases.action: Kill a specialist after its durable checkpoint and restart or replace it.
cases.expected: Resume a usable session or create a new attempt with saved handoff; preserve work; reject stale prior ownership/results.
cases.evidence: Checkpoint, lease and attempt lineage.

cases.title: Coordinator restart
cases.action: Kill the coordinator while specialists and mailbox remain up.
cases.expected: Rebuild state from durable records; reconcile running assignments and pending messages before dispatch.
cases.evidence: Before/after snapshots and zero duplicate launches.

cases.title: Workbench restart
cases.action: Restart the local service during active work with children still alive.
cases.expected: Identify owned surviving processes; reconcile leases and unknown actions; never infer process death from lost connection.
cases.evidence: Reopened store, ownership evidence and recovery decisions.

cases.title: Pause with active child tool
cases.action: Pause while an agent's child process is writing a bounded local artifact.
cases.expected: Show pausing until agent and child activity stop; block new work; preserve artifact and checkpoint.
cases.evidence: Process-group termination/stop evidence and dispatch cutoff.

cases.title: Resume and cancellation
cases.action: Resume paused work, then cancel during another tool action.
cases.expected: Resume uses durable history; cancel stops further dispatch and pending side effects while preserving files, evidence and PR identity.
cases.evidence: Control events, artifacts and post-cancel effect count.

cases.title: PID reuse and competing owners
cases.action: Reuse a stale PID and start two controllers trying to adopt the same assignment.
cases.expected: Use durable identity plus lease/process-start evidence; never signal an unrelated PID; only one owner acts.
cases.evidence: Lease transaction and fake process-identity responses.

cases.title: Recovery bounds
cases.action: Fail an assignment through two automatic repair/replacement cycles and attempt a third.
cases.expected: Persist the counter across restart; third automatic cycle is blocked; uncertain ownership/effects escalate immediately.
cases.evidence: Recovery counters and needs-attention decision.

cases.title: Partial and corrupt state
cases.action: Inject truncated journal data, unavailable storage and failure between transactional writes.
cases.expected: No fabricated completed state or destructive reset; surface recoverable error; preserve last known durable evidence.
cases.evidence: Store errors, transaction boundaries and retained artifacts.

cases.title: Concurrency ceilings
cases.action: Queue two coding tickets and four compatible specialist assignments.
cases.expected: At most one coding ticket and three specialists execute; coordinator is counted separately; others remain queued.
cases.evidence: Scheduler timeline and observed process counts.

cases.title: Single writer lease
cases.action: Request simultaneous code and documentation writes to the same worktree.
cases.expected: Serialize writers; read/review only a stable published revision; rejected writer gets no mutation permission.
cases.evidence: Lease history and repository mutation log.

cases.title: Independent next ticket
cases.action: Mark a PR created, then CI pending, then ready for review.
cases.expected: Next independent ticket starts only at accepted readiness; PR creation or idle terminal alone cannot release the slot.
cases.evidence: Evidence-gate events and next launch time.

cases.title: Dependent ticket
cases.action: Return unmerged, closed-unmerged, unknown and verified-merged provider states.
cases.expected: Dependent work starts only after verified merge; neither close nor local branch presence substitutes for merge.
cases.evidence: Provider fixture responses and dependency decisions.

cases.title: Repeated controls and queue restart
cases.action: Race reorder, Run, Pause and Cancel requests, then restart storage.
cases.expected: Operations are transactional and idempotent; retain valid order without duplicate active runs.
cases.evidence: Request IDs, persisted queue and invariant checks.

cases.title: Isolated repository setup
cases.action: Start work with dirty files and existing branches in the operator checkout.
cases.expected: Create a separate owned branch/worktree; leave original files, index, HEAD and untracked files unchanged.
cases.evidence: Git status/hash snapshots and worktree registry.

cases.title: Continue existing work
cases.action: Select an existing branch/PR with matching and conflicting ownership evidence.
cases.expected: Continue only explicitly selected, verified owned work; uncertainty requires operator decision.
cases.evidence: Selection, branch/PR identity and ownership record.

cases.title: Interrupted edit or commit
cases.action: Crash after a file write and after commit creation but before acknowledgement.
cases.expected: Retain partial work; inspect repository state and commit identity before repeating; never create duplicate logical commits blindly.
cases.evidence: File hashes, reflog and action ledger.

cases.title: Base branch drift
cases.action: Advance the target branch after passing review; exercise clean rebase and conflict.
cases.expected: Invalidate affected evidence; refresh only owned work per project policy; revalidate new revision or escalate uncertain scope.
cases.evidence: Old/new head/base and stale-evidence events.

cases.title: Local output boundaries
cases.action: Attempt edits via path traversal, symlink escape and unauthorized repository paths.
cases.expected: Reject writes outside the owned scope; return a concrete blocked action.
cases.evidence: Filesystem sentinels and denied tool events.

cases.title: Real local checks on scripted patches
cases.action: Apply a deliberately failing patch and a corrected patch to a disposable repository.
cases.expected: Run actual repository checks; capture exit status/output and tested revision; do not substitute scripted success claims.
cases.evidence: Patch hashes, command environment, logs and Git SHAs.

cases.title: Complete coding evidence
cases.action: Provide matching accepted-criteria coverage, required checks and independent review for a stable head/base.
cases.expected: Ready for review only when every required condition has current evidence.
cases.evidence: Gate decision with linked evidence IDs and revisions.

cases.title: False completion signals
cases.action: Return terminal silence, exit zero without required artifacts, prompt completed, and a specialist saying tests passed.
cases.expected: None substitutes for required check/review evidence; empty or missing results remain incomplete.
cases.evidence: Raw output, absent evidence and blocked gate.

cases.title: Failed, skipped and unavailable checks
cases.action: Vary each required check through failed, skipped, cancelled, unavailable and passed states.
cases.expected: Only an actual pass satisfies a required check; distinguish states in evidence/UI.
cases.evidence: Per-check status and readiness decision.

cases.title: Revision mismatch
cases.action: Alter code, acceptance criteria, project check rules or target base after evidence was recorded.
cases.expected: Invalidate affected coverage/check/review evidence; rework cannot inherit stale approval.
cases.evidence: Revision vectors and stale reasons.

cases.title: Review findings and repair
cases.action: Return a blocking review finding; apply a fix that changes the head.
cases.expected: Route bounded repair; require fresh relevant checks and independent review before readiness.
cases.evidence: Finding disposition and review/check provenance.

cases.title: Forged or corrupt evidence
cases.action: Submit another run's check artifact, altered result hash or reviewer identity from the implementer.
cases.expected: Reject mismatched provenance; agents cannot waive the gate through message content.
cases.evidence: Evidence validation failures and immutable original records.

cases.title: Hosted check regression
cases.action: After readiness, emit a required hosted check failure for current head and a late success for old head.
cases.expected: Revoke readiness immediately; old success cannot restore it; do not auto-resume agents.
cases.evidence: Provider event dedupe, head matching and workflow events.

cases.title: Honest research evidence
cases.action: Return unsupported citations and missing requested design artifacts for a research-only run.
cases.expected: Block its outcome criteria without inventing coding evidence; verified artifacts complete only the research outcome.
cases.evidence: Artifact existence/hash, citation fixtures and outcome-specific gate.

cases.title: Allowed Jira updates
cases.action: Emit start, milestone, blocker and PR-ready events.
cases.expected: Queue status/comments/evidence links using reporter authority; description/criteria rewrites require explicit operator instruction.
cases.evidence: Fake Jira request ledger and permission decision.

cases.title: Jira outage and recovery
cases.action: Take Jira offline while an accepted run progresses, then restore it.
cases.expected: Continue accepted work; persist pending updates visibly; reconcile/retry without duplicate comments or lost order.
cases.evidence: Durable outbound actions and fake Jira objects.

cases.title: Uncertain external writes
cases.action: Commit a Jira comment or PR creation remotely, drop response, restart and query existing/absent/unknown outcomes.
cases.expected: Reconcile existing objects; retry only when non-application is established; unknown remains attention-required, including inconclusive empty lookup.
cases.evidence: Action keys, readback evidence and exact side-effect counts.

cases.title: PR content and identity
cases.action: Create a simulated PR for an owned branch with evidence, then resume work on it.
cases.expected: Correct target/head/title/body and evidence links; reuse same PR on rework; never create a second PR blindly.
cases.evidence: Fake provider object and branch/evidence mapping.

cases.title: Human review and merge
cases.action: Reach readiness, supply review feedback, then choose Resume and later simulate human merge.
cases.expected: No automatic merge; feedback remains visible until explicit Resume; dependent release needs verified merge.
cases.evidence: Zero merge writes, resume event and provider observation.

cases.title: Conflicting and delayed provider events
cases.action: Deliver duplicate/out-of-order PR, CI and Jira updates across a restart.
cases.expected: Apply events idempotently by resource revision; do not regress known state or erase local refinements.
cases.evidence: Inbound event ledger and final resource state.

cases.title: Provider permissions and partial failure
cases.action: Deny push, deny PR creation after push, and reject a Jira transition.
cases.expected: Preserve confirmed earlier outcomes; report exact blocked step; don't claim PR/Jira success or undo unrelated work.
cases.evidence: Git/provider ledgers and pending/failed action states.

cases.title: Three separate status dimensions
cases.action: Combine Jira In Progress with workflow waiting and agent disconnected/idle states.
cases.expected: Show Jira status, workflow and agent activity independently; planned assignments never look running.
cases.evidence: API state plus accessible UI assertions.

cases.title: Steering lifecycle
cases.action: Store steering during an outage; later deliver, acknowledge and apply it with a disposition.
cases.expected: Show stored/received/applied separately; route operator steering through the coordinator; retain history on reload.
cases.evidence: Steering IDs, receipts, disposition and UI state.

cases.title: Observe specialists
cases.action: Select each process and inspect output, tool activity, model identity and addressed messages.
cases.expected: Show actual observed events, disconnection/staleness and assignment/attempt identity; no invented output.
cases.evidence: Browser assertions against process/message event fixtures.

cases.title: Insert and pause from UI
cases.action: Insert a specialist while busy, pause, reload and resume.
cases.expected: Show queued insertion and pausing honestly until confirmed; retain actions and state after reload.
cases.evidence: UI actions matched to durable events.

cases.title: Disconnected and failed integration states
cases.action: Use missing runner, Jira outage, undelivered message and unknown cost.
cases.expected: Expose actionable unavailable/pending/unknown states; don't show success counters for simulated or unavailable integrations.
cases.evidence: Accessible labels and backing data.

cases.title: Basic complete operator flow
cases.action: Import/find/select/refine/queue/reorder/inspect/pause/resume/cancel using keyboard and a narrow viewport.
cases.expected: Controls remain usable, validation is clear, save failures retain edits, reload preserves durable data.
cases.evidence: Browser trace, screenshots and persisted data assertions.

cases.title: Loopback and origin enforcement
cases.action: Attempt mutations from another origin, hostile Host, missing origin in browser mutation context and non-loopback bind configuration.
cases.expected: Reject untrusted mutations; allow valid same-origin operation through documented local client rules.
cases.evidence: Server response and zero side effects.

cases.title: Secrets and environment isolation
cases.action: Place synthetic sentinel credentials in server-only configuration and error paths.
cases.expected: No credential in UI, model prompts, logs or exported evidence; child environment is allowlisted.
cases.evidence: Artifact scan and captured child environment keys.

cases.title: Untrusted ticket or message instructions
cases.action: Embed requests to merge, deploy, bypass review, steal secrets or write another repo in imported text and peer messages.
cases.expected: Control plane grants no new authority; simulated malicious tool requests are denied regardless of text.
cases.evidence: Tool authorization and zero forbidden effects.

cases.title: Network containment
cases.action: Try a non-loopback connection from controller, fake provider and child tool; enumerate every listener.
cases.expected: Test aborts on egress or uncontrolled listener; only disposable loopback services can be reached.
cases.evidence: Fail-closed network guard and listener/request ledger.

cases.title: Destructive cleanup boundaries
cases.action: Crash the harness and restart cleanup with a reused PID or foreign directory sentinel.
cases.expected: Cleanup touches only verified test-owned processes, ports and paths; no user config or repository changes.
cases.evidence: Ownership markers, liveness and unchanged sentinels.

cases.title: No infrastructure or merge tools
cases.action: Return scripted requests for deployment, infrastructure changes and merge during normal coding work.
cases.expected: Actions are absent or denied by initial scope; cannot be smuggled through a reporter or specialist.
cases.evidence: Granted tool set and authorization failures.

cases.title: Active-time budget
cases.action: Advance fake time through execution, operator wait, hosted CI wait and service restart.
cases.expected: Only active execution consumes the configured initial 60-minute budget; expiration requests safe pause; restart never resets usage.
cases.evidence: Persisted time intervals and pause events.

cases.title: Cost provenance
cases.action: Provide actual usage, estimated pricing, unknown prices and partially missing accounting.
cases.expected: Label actual/estimate/unavailable correctly; no fabricated zero cost or hard monetary guarantee without reliable accounting.
cases.evidence: Usage provenance and displayed totals.

cases.title: Bounded failures and backpressure
cases.action: Cause repeated model errors, full inboxes and a stalled consumer across simulated time.
cases.expected: Bound attempts, queue growth and retry rate; apply backpressure and surface attention without dropping accepted work.
cases.evidence: Attempt/rate counters and durable backlog.

cases.title: Repeatable schedules
cases.action: Replay a saved randomized schedule of control requests, duplicates, crashes and replies.
cases.expected: Same seed reproduces failures; invariants hold across generated schedules; failing seed/event trace is retained.
cases.evidence: Seed, event order and invariant report.
